terms.category: Relational Databases & Core System of Record

terms.oneLiner: The free, battle-tested database that holds your company's master records — orders, customers, stock — and refuses to lose them.
terms.notes: Runs under the permissive PostgreSQL Licence, free forever. PostgreSQL 18.x is the current stable line; PostgreSQL 19 Beta 4 was announced 2026-09-24. Nearly 40 years of continuous development from the 1986 UC Berkeley POSTGRES project. Cost trap: managed PostgreSQL bills hourly compute plus storage plus connection limits — self-hosting turns a variable cloud bill into a fixed one.
terms.origin: PostgreSQL Global Development Group (origin: UC Berkeley POSTGRES project, 1986) · PostgreSQL Licence

smartStack.label: The Free System of Record
smartStack.headline: Enterprise databases used to mean licence fees — PostgreSQL made the system of record free
smartStack.description: 'The company database' historically meant Oracle or SQL Server licences plus annual support contracts. PostgreSQL delivers the same ACID guarantees under a permissive licence, so the saved budget goes back into people and product.

newStack.note: PostGIS, pgvector and TimescaleDB extend it without a new vendor

newStack.label: Run it anywhere
newStack.note: Self-hosting makes the database bill a fixed, predictable cost

anatomy.desc: The 1986 UC Berkeley research project that became the most-adopted database on earth.
The universal query language every tool, report and analyst already speaks.
Rows and tables under strict rules, so money and stock counts can never be silently wrong.

terms.oneLiner: It bolts a time-focused engine onto PostgreSQL so you can ask 'what did the sensors, sales and servers do second by second?' without the database falling over.
terms.notes: Ships as a PostgreSQL extension rather than a separate database, so there is no new system to run and no data migration. Version 2.30.2 released 2026-09-29 and the current release line is 2.x. Vendor documentation recommends 8GB RAM for a production install, making sizing the real cost decision. Boardroom angle: telemetry is exactly what OEE and factory-fleet reporting depend on, and this is the cheapest credible path to it.
terms.origin: Timescale Inc. (Timescale License for TSL code, Apache 2.0 elsewhere)

smartStack.label: Time Data Without a Second Database
smartStack.headline: Sensor and event data used to need a whole extra database platform
smartStack.description: Adding a separate time-series vendor meant a second licence, a second on-call rotation and a second backup plan. TimescaleDB keeps the data inside PostgreSQL and turns it into a first-class citizen.

terms.oneLiner: It stores data like a spreadsheet column instead of a filing cabinet row, so questions across millions of rows get answered in seconds.
terms.notes: Apache-2.0 licensed and self-hostable, with an official ClickHouse Cloud. The 26.x stable release line is current, with 26.9.x builds published. The project's own description is an open-source column-oriented database management system that allows generating analytical data reports in real-time. Cost trap: columnar stores are fast to read but expensive to write row-by-row — feed them through a queue, not hundreds of individual inserts per second.

terms.oneLiner: A full SQL analytics engine that runs inside the program asking questions — no database server, no install, no monthly bill.
terms.notes: Written in C++ under the MIT licence, with first-class clients for Python, R, Java and WebAssembly; the current release line is 1.5.x. Runs entirely in-process, which makes it the cheapest credible way to let agents run real SQL analysis locally. Cost trap worth teaching: it is an analytical engine, not a multi-user write server — swapping it in as the system of record is the classic expensive mistake.

terms.full: Qdrant Vector Database and Search Engine
terms.logoSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M12 2 3 7v10l9 5 9-5V7l-9-5Z" stroke="#a78bfa" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3" stroke="#00e5ff" stroke-width="2"/></svg>
terms.oneLiner: A purpose-built search engine for AI meaning, written for speed at scale and filterable like a normal database.
terms.notes: Written in Rust and released under Apache-2.0; the current release line is 1.19.x (for example v1.19.1). It stores vectors and metadata together, so you can filter by tenant, date or product while searching semantically. Cost trap: per-vector storage charges scale with dimension count, so quantisation and dimensionality reduction are the levers that actually move the bill.

terms.logoSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="6" cy="18" r="3" stroke="#00e5ff" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="18" cy="18" r="3" stroke="#a78bfa" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="12" cy="5" r="3" stroke="#38bdf8" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M7.8 16 11 7.6M16.2 16 13 7.6M9 18h6" stroke="#a78bfa" stroke-width="1.6"/></svg>
terms.oneLiner: It stores data as a web of connected things and people, then answers relationship questions that ordinary tables make painfully slow.
terms.notes: The repository is GPL-3.0 with commercial licensing available from Neo4j, Inc.; created 2012-11-12 and written in Java. Its query language, Cypher, is the clearest way for a business to describe 'who knows whom, and through what'. Boardroom value: this is the engine behind agent memory and 'who introduced us' style answers — questions relational databases answer badly.
terms.origin: Neo4j, Inc. (originally Neo Technology, 2012) · GPL-3.0 with commercial enterprise edition

smartStack.label: Relationships Are the Real Data
smartStack.headline: Forcing relationships into flat tables is why knowledge tools get slow and brittle
smartStack.description: People, companies, parts and suppliers are defined by their links. Modelling links as first-class data is what makes agent memory and root-cause tracing answerable in one query.

terms.full: vLLM LLM Inference and Serving Engine
terms.logoSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="3" y="6" width="18" height="12" rx="2" stroke="#00e5ff" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M7 15V9l3 3 3-3v6M15 9v6h3" stroke="#a78bfa" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>
terms.oneLiner: It is the machine that actually runs your AI model on your own hardware, serving many users at once without wasting memory.
terms.notes: Repository created 2023-02-09, Apache-2.0, and self-describes as a high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs. Its headline technical contribution is PagedAttention, which manages the attention key/value cache the way an operating system virtualises memory — that is where the memory efficiency comes from, and it is the reason batching works so well. Cost trap: buying GPUs is a capital decision, and idle accelerators are pure burn; this is the term that determines your AI margin.
terms.origin: vLLM project / UC Berkeley Sky Computing Lab lineage (2023) · Apache-2.0

smartStack.label: Serve AI Without Wasting the Hardware
smartStack.headline: Serving an AI model naively wastes most of the expensive hardware you bought
smartStack.description: AI accelerators are the single most expensive line item in an AI product. Efficient serving is the difference between a sustainable margin and a runaway bill.

legacyStack.label: Wasted memory
legacyStack.note: Attention caches reserved at full size, leaving capacity unused

legacyStack.label: One user at a time
legacyStack.note: Expensive hardware sits idle between requests

legacyStack.label: Idle GPU spend
legacyStack.note: Accelerators bought and paid for but not serving traffic

newStack.label: PagedAttention
newStack.note: Attention memory is paged like virtual memory, cutting waste

newStack.label: Continuous batching
newStack.note: New requests join the running batch instead of waiting for it to finish

newStack.label: Apache-2.0 self-hosting
newStack.note: The serving engine is free; only the hardware costs money

anatomy.desc: The serving engine created for high-throughput LLM inference.
The model weights being served to many callers.
PagedAttention keeps the attention cache from wasting accelerator memory.

flow.title: Request Arrives
flow.desc: An application sends a completion request to the local server.

flow.title: Scheduler Batches
flow.desc: The engine adds the request to the running batch and allocates pages.

flow.title: Tokens Generated
flow.desc: The model produces output while other requests share the same hardware.

flow.title: Many Users Served
flow.desc: Throughput per GPU is maximised, cutting cost per answer.

replaces: Wasting accelerator memory on full-size caches

terms.logoSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M5 8c0-2 3-3 7-3s7 1 7 3-3 3-7 3-7-1-7-3Z" stroke="#00e5ff" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M5 12c0 2 3 3 7 3s7-1 7-3M5 16c0 2 3 3 7 3s7-1 7-3" stroke="#a78bfa" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
terms.oneLiner: It lets you download and run AI models privately on your own computer in one command — no cloud, no per-token bill, nothing leaving the building.
terms.notes: Repository created 2023-06-26, MIT-licensed and written in Go, describing itself as a way to 'get up and running' with models including Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Qwen and Gemma. Current release v0.35.1 (2026-09-29). Its role in the stack is developer velocity and data privacy: local inference for drafts, classification and sensitive documents before escalating to a hosted frontier model. Cost trap: local models are excellent for drafts and verification, and a poor substitute for a frontier model on hard reasoning — the failure mode is quality, not cost.
terms.origin: Ollama (2023) · MIT

smartStack.label: Private AI Without a Cloud Bill
smartStack.headline: Every AI call to the cloud is another line item and another privacy question
smartStack.description: Sending internal documents to an external API has both a cost and a compliance dimension. Running the model on your own hardware removes both concerns for routine work.

legacyStack.label: Every prompt leaves the building

legacyStack.label: Per-token billing on every task
legacyStack.note: Drafting, classifying and summarising all billed at API rates

legacyStack.label: Network dependency
legacyStack.note: No outbound connectivity means no AI capability at all

newStack.label: Models stay on your hardware
newStack.note: Prompts and documents never leave the machine

newStack.label: One-command operation
newStack.note: Pull a model and it is running locally

newStack.label: MIT licence, no per-call fee
newStack.note: Cost becomes fixed hardware rather than metered usage

A local endpoint that speaks the same style as hosted model APIs.

terms.category: Edge Routers, Reverse Proxies & API Gateways
terms.logoSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M3 17h6l3-9 3 9h6" stroke="#38bdf8" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="12" cy="17" r="2" fill="#00e5ff"/></svg>
terms.oneLiner: It is the front door of your software — it notices when a new service appears, gets it a public address and a security certificate, with no human configuring it.
terms.notes: Repository created 2015-09-13, MIT-licensed and Go-based, self-describing as a modern HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer that configures itself automatically from Docker, Swarm, Kubernetes, Consul, etcd, Rancher and Amazon ECS. Its own documentation states that pointing Traefik at your orchestrator should be the only configuration step needed. Current release v3.7.13 (2026-09-04). Cost trap: certificate automation and routing look free until you need fine-grained per-tenant rate limits — that is where a paid gateway tier usually wins.
terms.origin: Traefik Labs (originally Docker Inc. ecosystem, 2015) · MIT

smartStack.label: Self-Configuring Edge Routing
smartStack.headline: Manual routing tables and certificates rot the moment a service changes
smartStack.description: Every new microservice traditionally meant editing load balancer config and requesting a certificate. A proxy that watches the orchestrator removes that step entirely.

legacyStack.label: Hand-edited routing tables
legacyStack.note: Every service addition requires a config change and a restart

legacyStack.label: Manual certificate handling
legacyStack.note: Certificates renewed by hand or by fragile scheduled jobs

legacyStack.label: Stale routing rules
legacyStack.note: Removed services keep receiving traffic until someone notices

newStack.label: Watches the orchestrator
newStack.note: Services are discovered automatically from Docker or Kubernetes

newStack.label: Automatic certificates
newStack.note: TLS certificates issued and renewed without tickets or downtime

newStack.label: MIT core
newStack.note: Load balancing and routing carry no per-request licence fee

anatomy.desc: The MIT-licensed application proxy from Traefik Labs.
Fronts your services and routes each request to the right backend.
Understands container platforms and configures itself from them.

flow.title: Service Starts
flow.desc: A new container comes up behind the proxy.

flow.title: Discovered Automatically
flow.desc: Traefik watches the orchestrator and registers the route.

flow.title: Certificate Issued
flow.desc: A TLS certificate is obtained and renewed automatically.

flow.title: Traffic Routed
flow.desc: External requests reach the right service over encrypted HTTPS.

replaces: Stale routes sending traffic to dead services

terms.logoSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M4 18c3-1 4-4 5-7s3-5 7-5" stroke="#00e5ff" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="4" cy="18" r="2.2" stroke="#a78bfa" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="16" cy="6" r="2.2" stroke="#a78bfa" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M16 16a4 4 0 0 0 4-4V9" stroke="#10b981" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
terms.oneLiner: It turns your scattered computers and servers into one private network — each device reachable by name from anywhere, with no firewall ports opened on the internet.
terms.notes: Repository created 2020-01-31, BSD-3-Clause licensed and Go-based, describing itself as 'the easiest, most secure way to use WireGuard and 2FA'. Current release v1.102.5 (2026-09-29). The architectural claim worth explaining to a board is that it is built on WireGuard, whose design is a deliberate simplification of the older VPN standards rather than a new protocol invented for marketing. Cost trap: the consumer model is per-user pricing, which is cheap for small teams and expensive for large distributed workforces — the crossover point is worth checking before a company-wide rollout.
terms.origin: Tailscale Inc. (Brad Boudreaux and David Knowles, 2020) · BSD-3-Clause, built on WireGuard

smartStack.label: Private Networks Without Firewall Punching
smartStack.headline: Traditional VPNs require opening ports and exposing services to the internet
smartStack.description: Remote access used to mean either a VPN concentrator bottleneck or exposed services with public addresses. A mesh network keeps traffic encrypted end to end without either.

legacyStack.label: Open firewall ports
legacyStack.note: Services are published straight to the internet to be reachable

legacyStack.label: Central VPN concentrator
legacyStack.note: All remote traffic funnels through one bottleneck that also sees plaintext

legacyStack.label: Shared credentials
legacyStack.note: One VPN account and password shared across an entire team

newStack.label: Peer-to-peer encryption
newStack.note: Traffic is encrypted directly between devices, WireGuard-based

newStack.label: Identity per device
newStack.note: Each machine authenticates itself, with 2FA and revocation per device

newStack.label: No inbound ports
newStack.note: Devices stay behind firewalls while still being reachable by name

anatomy.desc: The BSD-licensed mesh VPN built on WireGuard.
Device identity and end-to-end encryption replace shared credentials.
Every device joins one private address space as if on the same office LAN.

flow.title: Device Joins
flow.desc: A laptop or server authenticates and joins the private network.

flow.title: Encrypted Tunnel Established
flow.desc: A WireGuard-based encrypted path opens to the peer.

flow.title: Name Resolution
flow.desc: The device is reachable by a stable private name anywhere.

flow.title: Access Revocable
flow.desc: Removing a device revokes its access immediately.

replaces: Opening inbound firewall ports to the internet
